contract: Road user a has made a turn to the left through region r, recognized as it leaves r. The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r. The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it. At that observation the heading change of a since its entry into r, in degrees and positive to the left, integrated from its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) with no interval between consecutive observations longer than step, lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive, so that a passage whose heading changes too little to be a turn and a reversal of direction both lie outside it. Conduct before the entry is not read. It denotes the change of a's heading between its entry into r and its exit only: it says nothing of the lanes a uses, of its speed, of its class, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a passage through r whose heading change is below turn_min, such as one straight through or a turn to the right; a heading change of u_turn_min or more, which is a reversal of direction; an observation at which a is still in r. Where the entry was not observed (it lies before the recording, or a's overlap with r was unknown at an observation since), where an interval between consecutive observations since the observation before the entry is longer than step, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing, it is unknown.

params.name: step
params.meaning: the largest interval between consecutive observations across which the heading change is integrated: the sampling standard of the integration, not a window and not a bound on how long ago the entry lies

params.name: turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change to the left between entry and exit at which the passage counts as a turn rather than a passage straight through

params.name: u_turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change magnitude at which the passage counts as a reversal of direction rather than a turn

elements.span: a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies)
elements.justification: rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" — its rise marks the entry into r and its fall the exit; it is footprint overlap, not distance, so neither nearness nor geometry stands for it.

kin.yaw_rate: "rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)"; the formula language's heading change since a formula last became true (headingSince, onset the rise of the overlap with r) integrates it. Not a stand-in for road curvature: the concept reads the road user's own turning, not the road's.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Region r is an intersection region. Road user a enters r heading east, its yaw rate observed at every scene at the sampling standard, turns a quarter turn to the left and leaves r heading north; at the exit observation its heading change since the entry lies in the band, so the concept holds there.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: Same region; a enters r heading east, turns a quarter turn to the right and leaves r heading south: the heading change since the entry is negative, below turn_min, so the concept does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in holds, but the source supplies no yaw rate for a: the heading change since the entry cannot be integrated and the concept is unknown at the exit.

contract: Road user a has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction" through region r, "whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not", recognized as it leaves r. The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r. The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it. At that observation the magnitude of the heading change of a since its entry into r, in degrees and positive to the left, integrated from its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) with no interval between consecutive observations longer than step, lies in the band from u_turn_min to a full turn minus u_turn_min, both inclusive, so that a turn short of a reversal and a full loop both lie outside it; a reversal to either hand is denoted, and one made in several movements, with halts or backing between them inside r, is denoted where its integrated heading change lies in the band. Conduct before the entry is not read. It denotes the change of a's heading between its entry into r and its exit only: it says nothing of the lanes a uses, of its speed, of its class, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a passage through r whose heading change magnitude is below u_turn_min, such as a turn to the left or the right or a passage straight through; a heading change magnitude above a full turn minus u_turn_min, which is a loop; an observation at which a is still in r. Where the entry was not observed (it lies before the recording, or a's overlap with r was unknown at an observation since), where an interval between consecutive observations since the observation before the entry is longer than step, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing, it is unknown.

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to
the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
The operator of a vehicle
who intends to exit a roundabout
Shall use the left lane to turn left or complete a U-turn

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed as one atom, never expanded; its exclusions are the reading's classification. "within a roundabout": st.roundabout "a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches" carries DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ("an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway", including the crosswalks on the entering and exiting roadways) at its whole extent; rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" anchors the subject to that roundabout, so no other roundabout of the scene is read. Same mapping as the index for "the operation of vehicles" and "within a roundabout".

"a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The operator" names who controls it, a relational role and no aggregate, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Same mapping as the index entry "The operator of a vehicle".

The intention to exit is not observable; it is read through the exit it leads to (observable_reading intention): the observation at which the subject's footprint (rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region") ceases to overlap the roundabout r (st.roundabout) it occupied, which is the recognition of the turn concepts ("The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r"). No declared intention: the words state an intention to exit, which is read by the exit made, and the turn they name is read by the heading change the concepts measure.

"to turn left or complete a U-turn": drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ("a turn to the left through region r ... heading change ... from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive") and drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ("so as to proceed in the opposite direction" through r), taking r = the roundabout the subject exits; a heading change measured from the entry into the roundabout to the exit is the turn the vehicle makes by the roundabout, whatever the circulation in between. "use the left lane": st.lane "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles" with st.lane_adjacency "lane ordinal within the carriageway ... ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction": the left lane is the lane of ordinal 1; rel.occupies anchors the lanes the subject's footprint overlaps. Not a stand-in exclusions: lane membership is read by footprint overlap and ordinal, never by a lateral offset from the edge, and the ordinal is not the marking between lanes.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). Bind a region r of kind st.roundabout. At the judged observation the subject exits r having turned left or completed a U-turn through it: drv_motion_left_turn_through_region(subject, r) or drv_motion_u_turn_through_region(subject, r) holds, each with step .param p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph and turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min (the U-turn concept takes step and u_turn_min only). The intention to exit is read through this exit.
obligation: Re-bind the same roundabout: a region r of kind st.roundabout for which the same concept holds for the subject at the judged observation. The subject used the left lane within r: at every observation from its entry into r (the latest observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose) up to the judged observation, wherever rel.occupies(subject, r) holds, every region l of kind st.lane with rel.occupies(subject, l) has st_lane_adjacency_ordinal(l) = 1. Written with since: since(phi, rises(occupies(subject, r)) and phi), phi = occupies(subject, r) implies forall lane l (occupies(subject, l) implies ordinal(l) = 1). Unknown where the entry lies before the recording or an ordinal of an occupied lane is unobserved.

narrowings.why: "The operator" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.

"who intends to exit a roundabout" is read through the exit itself: the duty is judged at the observation at which the vehicle leaves the roundabout, the recognition of the turn; a vehicle that intends to exit but has not yet left is judged when it leaves.

"use the left lane" is read as occupying, within the roundabout, no lane other than the lane of ordinal 1 of its carriageway from the entry to the exit; a footprint straddling the left lane and another lane is not use of the left lane alone. A single-lane roundabout's only lane is ordinal 1.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A two-lane roundabout r (st.roundabout) whose circulatory and approach lanes carry st.lane_adjacency ordinals 1 (inner, leftmost) and 2 (outer). The subject, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle), enters r heading east in the lane of ordinal 2, circulates counter-clockwise in the outer lane and leaves r heading north: its yaw rate, observed at every scene at the sampling standard, integrates to a quarter turn to the left since the entry. At the exit the left turn through r is recognized; the subject occupied a lane of ordinal 2 within r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout and the same left turn, but the subject enters and circulates in the lane of ordinal 1 only and leaves r heading north.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 2 and leaves at the first exit heading south, a quarter turn to the right since the entry: no left turn or U-turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply lane ordinals (st.lane_adjacency absent): which lane the subject used is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 2, circulates and leaves heading west, a half turn to the left since the entry: a U-turn through r made from the outer lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject makes the U-turn of branch_1 in the lane of ordinal 1 throughout.

onset.words: the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
onset.justification: The act begins at the subject's entry into the roundabout: the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose, the onset the concepts declare ("its entry into r").

occasion.recognition: who intends to exit a roundabout

under_way.words: to turn left or complete a U-turn
under_way.justification: Inside the act the subject's heading change since its entry into r (headingSince, integrated from kin.yaw_rate "rate of change of heading") is defined and the subject's footprint overlaps r; before the entry it is not. The heading's integration reads the subject's motion, not the place alone.

the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
The operator of a vehicle
who intends to exit a roundabout

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed as one atom. segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled, any vehicle,
to fail to stop not less than fifty feet from the nearest side of
a school pedestrian lane
where any signal device, flagman or other person is stationed, giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing the street;

and it is further declared unlawful to proceed until such signal has stopped, raised, or been removed, or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane has given a signal to go, or has left the locality.

elements.justification: "any vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom, never expanded. "any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled" names who controls the vehicle, read through its controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

"stop" here is a stop the law requires, so the definition whose own scope is "when required" (DEF-NRS-484A-255, "complete cessation from movement") is the one whose scope the words meet; drv.motion.complete_halt carries it ("The road user is at rest at the observation ... at or below a tolerance the caller sets for the source's speed resolution"). "not less than fifty feet from the nearest side of" the crossing: st.region_geometry "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)" is the distance from the vehicle's body to the nearest side of the crosswalk region, a distance the words themselves state (literal); it is not used for occupancy, so the "Not a stand-in for: occupancy" clause does not apply.

"a school pedestrian lane": st.crosswalk "marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection" — a lane for pedestrians to cross the street; not a sidewalk. Its school character is read through the warning of children crossing given there (observable_reading status). "the street" it crosses: st.on_way "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on" ties the crosswalk to the highway (st.highway, "the entire public way between its boundary lines") on which the subject's governed travel region also lies; st.on_way is not nearness. The crosswalk is the one the subject approaches: prim.region_offset_along "the signed distance ... from a road user's reference point ... to a structure region ... measured along a carrier's designated direction" positive puts it ahead of the subject along its travel region's direction; the primitive establishes only the side, and the nearest side's distance is read from st.region_geometry, as its contract requires.

"any signal device ... giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing": dev.crossing_warning_signal "a signal device at a pedestrian or school crossing that warns of persons crossing; active attribute" with active true. "flagman or other person is stationed, giving warning": dev.human_direction "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}" of any role ("or other person"), indication stop, the warning that halts traffic. "stationed" at the crossing the subject approaches is read through dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls" on the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"): a device governing the subject's travel region and a crosswalk ahead of it on the same way. dev.governs is not a position, and the halt place is read from the crosswalk, not from the device.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The duty arises at an event: at the judged observation t the subject comes within fifty feet of a crosswalk at which a warning is given. Bind a travel region g (kind st.travel_region) with rel.occupies(subject, g); a device d with dev.governs(d, g) that gives warning at t: a dev.crossing_warning_signal whose active attribute holds, or a dev.human_direction of any role whose indication is stop; a highway w (st.highway) with st.on_way(g, w); a crosswalk c (st.crosswalk) with st.on_way(c, w), ahead of the subject along g (prim.region_offset_along(subject, c, g) > 0), and the nearest such crosswalk ahead (no other crosswalk on w has a smaller positive offset along g). The event: st_region_geometry_distance(subject, c) is below the literal fifty feet at t and was at or above it at the observation before (rises of the distance being below fifty feet).
obligation: Duty of rule 4c. Act: a halt of the subject (drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation at which the body distance st_region_geometry_distance(subject, c) is at or above the literal fifty feet, c is ahead of the subject along a travel region it occupies that d governs, and d gives warning. Search: back from t through observations at which d gives warning continuously and c stays ahead of the subject along a travel region it occupies that d governs. The search ends at the onset of d's warning (the observation at which d's warning rose: a halt before the warning began is no halt for it), at the previous occurrence of the same event for the same subject and crosswalk (an earlier rise of 'within fifty feet of c'), or at an observation at which c is not ahead. Written: since(warning(d) and ahead(c) and not earlier-event, halt(subject) and distance(subject, c) >= fifty feet and warning(d) and ahead(c)). Where the search finds the halt, compliant; where it reaches the warning's onset, the previous event or an observation with c not ahead without the halt, violated; where it reaches the start of the recording with d warning and c ahead at every observation and no halt found, unknown. A missing distance, governance or direction makes the duty unknown only where the verdict turns on it.

narrowings.why: "any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.
The crosswalk is a school pedestrian lane where the warning of children crossing is given there; the school designation is read through that warning, not through a separate designation.

"that children are about to cross or are crossing" is read through the warning given, not through children observed: the device's or person's warning (signal active, or a person's stop indication) is the evidence of the crossing it announces; the device stationed at the pedestrian lane is the one governing the subject's travel region with that lane the nearest crosswalk ahead on the same way.

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled, any vehicle,
to fail to stop not less than fifty feet from the nearest side of
a school pedestrian lane
where any signal device, flagman or other person is stationed, giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing the street;
and it is further declared unlawful to proceed
until such signal has stopped, raised, or been removed, or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane has given a signal to go, or has left the locality.

elements.justification: "any vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom; the driving person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

"to proceed" refers to the stop the first clause requires, with its qualification kept: a halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, carrying DEF-NRS-484A-255 "complete cessation from movement", the definition whose scope is a stop "when required") made while the body distance to the crosswalk (st.region_geometry "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it") is not less than fifty feet, under the warning. The first clause's duty itself is node LVMC_11_46_030_o1; here the stop is the act this duty follows, carried in full, not the other rule's verdict.

Same words, same atoms as LVMC_11_46_030_o1: st.crosswalk "marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks" on the street (st.on_way to the st.highway the subject's travel region lies on), ahead of the subject along its travel region by prim.region_offset_along (positive, the side only).

Same words, same atoms as LVMC_11_46_030_o1: dev.crossing_warning_signal with active true, or dev.human_direction of any role with indication stop, governing (dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

"unlawful to proceed": the vehicle stays at rest; drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation ... speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance") failing is any movement after the stop. Not denoted by the concept: why it stays.

"until such signal has stopped, raised, or been removed": the same dev.crossing_warning_signal d no longer has its active attribute, or is no longer in the scene or no longer governs the subject's travel region (dev.governs). "or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane has given a signal to go": the same dev.human_direction d shows indication proceed ("indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}"). "or has left the locality": d is no longer in the scene or no longer governs the subject's travel region. "such" singles out the device that gave the warning the subject stopped for; each end condition reads that device.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). At the judged observation bind, as in LVMC_11_46_030_o1, a travel region g with rel.occupies(subject, g), a device d with dev.governs(d, g) giving warning (dev.crossing_warning_signal active, or dev.human_direction of any role with indication stop), a highway w with st.on_way(g, w), and the nearest crosswalk c on w ahead of the subject along g (prim.region_offset_along(subject, c, g) > 0). The subject stopped for that warning and the warning has lasted since: since(warning(d) and ahead(c), drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) and st_region_geometry_distance(subject, c) >= the literal fifty feet and warning(d) and ahead(c)), with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance. The duty ends ('until') at the first observation at which d gives no warning: the signal's active attribute is false or the signal is gone or no longer governs g ('stopped, raised, or been removed'); the person's indication is proceed ('a signal to go'), or the person is gone or no longer governs g ('has left the locality'); from then the since fails and the duty does not apply.
obligation: The subject does not proceed: drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) holds at the judged observation, with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance.

narrowings.why: "any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The school pedestrian lane is the crosswalk at which the warning of children crossing is given; the school designation is read through that warning.

"stationed" at the pedestrian lane is read as a warning device or person governing the subject's travel region, the lane being the nearest crosswalk ahead on the same way; "children are about to cross or are crossing" is read through the warning given.
"proceed" is read as any movement above the halt tolerance after the stop, forward or not.

segmentation.text: No vehicle
in excess of eight thousand pounds unladen weight
shall be operated or moved
upon any street
(other than a truck route),
in any residence district
between the hours of seven p.m. and six a.m.;

provided, however, that the Department of Public Works may, at its discretion, upon application in writing, issue a special permit in writing authorizing the applicant to operate or move such vehicle between the hours of seven p.m. and six a.m. In issuing such permit, the Department may impose such conditions thereon, such as routes to be followed, time of operation or movement, or other matters, as it deems necessary or desirable.

elements.justification: "vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom, never expanded.

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on this span): ru.commercial_motor_vehicle is "vehicle over the jurisdiction's commercial mass class or marked as commercially licensed" — a class, not the stated unladen weight, and a vehicle over the law's figure need not be commercially classed; ru.truck is "motor vehicle for carrying goods, with a body built for that purpose" — a body type, not a weight. No atom carries a vehicle's unladen weight.

"shall be operated or moved": the vehicle not moving; drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation ... speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance") failing is a movement of the vehicle. "operated" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

"street" (DEF-NRS-484A-265, "the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city"): st.highway "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders" at its whole extent, the city limit being the reading's scope for a city ordinance; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index entry "upon a street". Not the roadway alone.

"a truck route": the designation is marked on the road by a sign, so the sign is the atom (ontology §9): dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route ("a point regulation by catalogue code ... truck_route") governing (dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). The sign's presence is the evidence of the designation (observable_reading status). "truck" here qualifies the route, not the road users the duty concerns.

"between the hours of seven p.m. and six a.m.": env.civil_time "the local calendar time of the observation: date, weekday, time of day" at or after the evening literal or before the morning literal. Not kin.time, which carries no time of day.

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on this span): ru.official_vehicle is "a vehicle in official or contracted road service" — not a vehicle holding a special permit; ru.commercial_motor_vehicle is "marked as commercially licensed" — a licence class, not a permit to move at night with its routes and hours. No atom carries a written permit issued for a vehicle.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose unladen weight exceeds the law's figure (gap: no atom carries it). At the judged observation it occupies a highway region (rel.occupies, st.highway); asm.residence_district holds; env.civil_time is at or after the evening literal (seven p.m.) or before the morning literal (six a.m.). Exception: no travel region it occupies is governed by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route. Exception: the vehicle does not move under a special permit (gap: no atom carries it).
obligation: The subject is not moved: drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) holds, with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance.

narrowings.why: "operated or moved" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a movement above the halt tolerance; an engine running at rest is not read as operation.
A truck route is read through the truck_route sign governing the subject's travel region; its presence is the evidence of the designation.

gaps.proposal: `ru.unladen_weight` | the mass of a vehicle without its load, as registered for it or as the source measures it (an attribute of a road user, kg) **Not a stand-in for:** the laden or gross mass, or a vehicle class such as a truck or a commercial vehicle | general — it decides which road users the night-time prohibition concerns
gaps.nearest: ru.commercial_motor_vehicle — "over the jurisdiction's commercial mass class or marked as commercially licensed": a class, not a stated unladen weight; ru.truck — "with a body built for that purpose": a body type, not a weight

gaps.proposal: `ru.special_permit` | a vehicle moving under a written special permit an authority has issued for it, with the permit's routes, hours and conditions as a structured attribute, as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a vehicle class or an official vehicle | local — it decides which road users the prohibition excuses

segmentation.text: Streets
other than truck routes
shall not be used as through routes
from one truck route to another
unless pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute

elements.justification: "Streets" (DEF-NRS-484A-265, "the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city"): st.highway "the entire public way between its boundary lines" at its whole extent, the city limit being the reading's scope for a city ordinance; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index entry "upon a street".

"other than truck routes": a street stretch on which no travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route; the designation is marked by the sign, so the sign is the atom (ontology §9), its presence the evidence (observable_reading status).

"used as through routes": the subject travels the street stretch (rel.occupies of st.highway regions with no truck route governing, at every observation of the stretch) from leaving one truck route to entering another, read through its controlled motion; the stretch is bounded by the two truck-route occupancies, so the history read is the stretch itself, not the recording.

"truck route": the routes designated for trucks; the road users a through-route ban between truck routes concerns are trucks, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck ("every motor vehicle which is used for the transportation or delivery of goods with a body built and designed for that purpose"), one atom. "from one truck route to another": the subject occupied (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route, and now comes to occupy one so governed that lies on a different way: st.on_way "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on" names the highway (st.highway) each lies on, and "another" is read as no highway in common between the two; st.on_way is not nearness.

"pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute": a purpose, read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): a halt on the stretch long enough to serve a stop, drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration") at some observation of the stretch, with min_duration the shortest pick-up or delivery dwell. A halt in traffic, shorter than that, is not such a stop.

applicability: The subject is a truck (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck). Let onTR(g) = rel.occupies(subject, g) for a travel region g governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route. Trigger: at the judged observation t the subject comes onto a truck route: some travel region g2 with onTR(g2) at t, and the subject occupied no truck-route-governed travel region at the observation before. Exception: within the stretch defined in the obligation, drv_motion_parked(subject) held at some observation (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.delivery_halt_min_duration); the exception reads the same stretch, re-bound with its full selection.
obligation: The subject did not use streets as a through route from one truck route to another: it is not the case that, going back from the observation before t, the subject occupied at every observation a highway region (st.highway) and no truck-route-governed travel region, back to an observation s at which it occupied a truck-route-governed travel region g1 such that no highway w has both st.on_way(g1, w) and st.on_way(g2, w). Written at t with since: not since((not onTR-any and occupies some st.highway) or rises(onTR-any), exists g1 (onTR(g1) and forall w (on_way(g1, w) implies not on_way(g2, w)))). Unknown where the stretch reaches the start of the recording; a stretch that began on the same truck route's way, or not on a truck route, is no through route.

narrowings.why: "used as through routes" is read as a continuous stretch on streets off truck routes between leaving a truck-route region and entering one on a highway the first does not lie on; a stretch that returns to the same truck route's way is no through route.
Truck routes are read through the truck_route sign governing the travel region; its presence is the evidence of the designation.

"pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute" is read through a halt on the stretch at least as long as the shortest pick-up or delivery dwell; the requirement itself and an essential use without such a halt are not observable.

segmentation.text: The parking of vehicles is prohibited or restricted in certain zones as set forth in this Section.

The location of such zones shall be established by posting appropriate signage or other durable markings, by painting curbs or the edges of road surfaces in accordance with the colors listed below, or by a combination thereof:
Red indicates no stopping, standing or parking,
whether or not the vehicle is attended and whether or not the engine or motor is running,
subject to the following:
(1) Except as provided in this Subsection,
a curb or road surface edge which is painted red indicates no parking,
whether or not accompanied by signage to that effect.
(2) When the location is accompanied by signage which indicates that parking is limited to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos,
those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes for the loading or unloading of passengers. (3)
When the location is accompanied by signage which indicates that parking is limited to RTC buses,
those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes for the loading or unloading of passengers. (4)
Armored cars and emergency vehicles may park at such locations
for the period necessary to conduct their business,
whether or not there is accompanying signage so indicating.
(5) At locations where a drop box for U.S. mail is adjacent to a curb or road surface painted red,
a person may stop
for the period of time necessary to expeditiously deposit mail in such a drop box.

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom, never expanded; the zones the sentence introduces are read by the spans that state them.

The zones are established by signage, durable markings or painted curbs and road-surface edges: st.curb_zone "a signed or marked length of curb; kind ...; colour ∈ {red, yellow, white, blue, gray, none} where the curb itself is painted" is such a zone, its presence the evidence that it is established (observable_reading status); rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... curb zone ...)" anchors the subject in the zone, so no other zone of the scene is read.

"Red": the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.curb_zone whose colour is red. "no stopping": "stopping" is DEF-NRS-484A-260 ("any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not"), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation") at any duration; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts too, so their purpose exclusions add nothing once every halt is barred. The definition's exclusion the concept does not make is carried beside it: "except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" — another road user ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane "a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane") within a queue gap of the bodies (rel.surface_gap "distance between the nearest points of two bodies", not centre distance); "or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device" — a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal showing a red indication (circular_red, red_arrow(dir), flashing_red), or a dev.stop_sign, governing (dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies. dev.governs is not a position.

"a curb or road surface edge which is painted red": st.curb_zone with colour red ("colour ... where the curb itself is painted"), the subject anchored by rel.occupies. The no-parking it restates is contained in the no-stopping of s3, so it adds no second duty.

"signage which indicates that parking is limited to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos": the red zone the subject occupies is of st.curb_zone kind tour_bus_loading ("a signed or marked length of curb; kind ∈ {..., tour_bus_loading, ...}"), its signage the evidence (observable_reading status). "tour buses, shuttle buses and limos" are the admitted aggregates DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus, DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::shuttle_bus and DEF-LVMC-11-02-090::limo, each one atom, never replaced by ru.tour_bus_or_limousine.

"those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes": the time since the subject came to rest in the zone (sinceRise of drv.motion.complete_halt and rel.occupies of the zone) is at most the literal thirty minutes. "for the loading or unloading of passengers" is a purpose read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose).

"signage which indicates that parking is limited to RTC buses": the red zone is of st.curb_zone kind bus_stop ("a signed or marked length of curb; kind ∈ {..., bus_stop, ...}"), the length of curb signed for buses, its signage the evidence (observable_reading status). "RTC buses" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-120::rtc_bus, one atom, never replaced by ru.transit_bus.
Same as s10: the time since the subject came to rest in the zone is at most the literal thirty minutes; the passenger purpose is read through the halt (observable_reading purpose).

"Armored cars": ru.official_vehicle with kind armored_car ("kind ∈ {..., armored_car, ...}"); "emergency vehicles": ru.emergency_vehicle ("vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency"), the class the words name, not a responding vehicle, so the "responding" exclusion does not apply. "may park at such locations": their halt (drv.motion.complete_halt) in the red zone.

"for the period necessary to conduct their business": a purpose, read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose): the armored car's or emergency vehicle's halt in the zone, whatever its length.

"a drop box for U.S. mail": st.obstruction kind mail_drop_box ("a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind ∈ {..., mail_drop_box, ...}"). "At locations where [it] is adjacent to a curb ... painted red": the subject, in the red zone, has its body within a reach of the drop box (st.region_geometry "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it"); a reach relating the box to the road user, not a relation between two regions; geometry is not used for occupancy.

"a person may stop": the vehicle's halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, "at rest at the observation"), the person read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). "stop" is a halting under both posted definitions.

operationalizations.standard: for the period of time necessary to expeditiously deposit mail in such a drop box
operationalizations.convention: curbside dwell of a single drop-off: the time to pull up, reach the box from the vehicle or a step away and post the mail; the halt counts as expeditious while the time since the subject came to rest in the zone (sinceRise of drv.motion.complete_halt and rel.occupies) is at most the parameter

residues.why: "whether or not the vehicle is attended and whether or not the engine or motor is running" makes the duty the same in every case: the halt is barred either way, so neither occupancy nor kin.engine_running is read.
"whether or not accompanied by signage to that effect": the red paint alone marks the zone; a sign beside it changes nothing.
"whether or not there is accompanying signage so indicating": the armored car and emergency vehicle exception holds with or without a sign.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). At the judged observation bind a region z of kind st.curb_zone whose colour is red, with rel.occupies(subject, z). Exceptions (the duty does not apply): (2) the subject is a tour bus, shuttle bus or limo (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus, DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::shuttle_bus or DEF-LVMC-11-02-090::limo), z is of kind tour_bus_loading, and Term.sinceRise(drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) and rel.occupies(subject, z)) is at most the literal thirty minutes; (3) the subject is an RTC bus (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-120::rtc_bus), z is of kind bus_stop, and the same time is at most the literal thirty minutes; (4) the subject is a ru.official_vehicle of kind armored_car or a ru.emergency_vehicle; (5) some st.obstruction o of kind mail_drop_box has st_region_geometry_distance(subject, o) at most p.mail_drop_box_reach, and the time since the subject came to rest in z is at most p.mail_deposit_max_halt. Each halt-duration test is unknown where the halt began before the recording.
obligation: The subject does not stop in z otherwise than as the definition of stopping excludes: drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) implies (some road user u, not the subject, with rel.ahead_behind_in_lane(u ahead of subject) and rel_surface_gap(subject, u) at most p.queue_halt_gap) or (some device governing a travel region the subject occupies directs a halt: a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, red_arrow(dir) or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign).

narrowings.why: The zones' establishment by sign, marking or paint is read through the signed or marked curb zone's presence.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" in the definition of stopping is read as a halt with another road user ahead in the subject's lane within the queue gap; a conflict that does not show as a road user ahead in the lane is not read. The officer's or device's direction is read as a stop indication, a red signal indication or a stop sign governing the subject's travel region.
Signage limiting parking to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos is read through the curb zone's kind tour_bus_loading.
"for the loading or unloading of passengers" is read through the halt it explains; whether passengers board is not read.

segmentation.text: The parking of vehicles is prohibited or restricted in certain zones as set forth in this Section.

The location of such zones shall be established by posting appropriate signage or other durable markings, by painting curbs or the edges of road surfaces in accordance with the colors listed below, or by a combination thereof:
Yellow indicates a zone for:
(1) Commercial vehicles to stop, stand or park for the purpose of loading or unloading freight
in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign; and
(2) Taxicabs to stop, stand, park for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for passengers
in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign.

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom; "is prohibited or restricted in certain zones" introduces the restriction the yellow zone states.

Same words, same atoms as LVMC_11_52_030_A: st.curb_zone "a signed or marked length of curb; ... colour ... where the curb itself is painted", its presence the evidence of the zone (observable_reading status); rel.occupies anchors the subject in it.

"Yellow indicates a zone for" the uses listed: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.curb_zone of colour yellow; the zone being for those uses only, any other halt in it (drv.motion.complete_halt, "at rest at the observation") is restricted. "stop" in the list carries two posted definitions, each with its own scope; both are a halting, which is what the concept reads, so no choice between them is made.

"Commercial vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-070::commercial_vehicle, one atom, never replaced by ru.commercial_motor_vehicle. "to stop, stand or park": its halt (drv.motion.complete_halt). "for the purpose of loading or unloading freight" is a purpose, read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose).

"an accompanying sign": a dev.zone_sign of kind parking_restricted ("a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; ... conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend — a list of time windows ..., a duration limit, a vehicle class") governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), the lane beside the curb. "in accordance with the conditions and times posted": prim.conditions_hold "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user" for the subject; the sign's legend is not whether its condition holds, which is the primitive's.

"Taxicabs" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab, one atom, never replaced by ru.taxicab. "to stop, stand, park": its halt (drv.motion.complete_halt). "for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for passengers" is read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose).
Same words, same atoms as s5: a dev.zone_sign of kind parking_restricted governing a travel region the subject occupies, with prim.conditions_hold for the subject.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). At the judged observation bind a region z of kind st.curb_zone whose colour is yellow, with rel.occupies(subject, z). Exceptions (the duty does not apply): (1) the subject is a commercial vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-070::commercial_vehicle) and some dev.zone_sign d of kind parking_restricted governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies, with prim.conditions_hold(d, subject); (2) the subject is a taxicab (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab) and such a sign's conditions hold for it.
obligation: The subject does not halt in z: not drv_motion_complete_halt(subject), with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance.

narrowings.why: The zones' establishment by sign, marking or paint is read through the signed or marked curb zone's presence.

"a zone for" commercial vehicles and taxicabs is read as barring any other vehicle's halt in the yellow zone, and theirs where the accompanying sign's conditions do not hold; a halt outside the sign's hours is read as outside the conditions posted.
"for the purpose of loading or unloading freight" is read through the commercial vehicle's halt; whether freight moves is not read.
The accompanying sign is read as a parking_restricted zone sign governing the lane beside the curb the subject occupies; its posting is the evidence of its force.
"for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for passengers" is read through the taxicab's halt.
The accompanying sign is read as a parking_restricted zone sign governing the lane beside the curb the subject occupies.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter:
No person shall stand or park a vehicle
in a roadway
other than parallel with the edge of the roadway headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement.

elements.justification: "Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter": no node of the corpus states such a provision; what the Chapter otherwise provides for the position of a standing vehicle shows on the road as posted angle parking: a dev.regulatory_sign with code angle_parking ("a point regulation by catalogue code ... angle_parking") governing (dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre.

"a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one atom. "stand or park": "stand" (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers") and "park" (DEF-NRS-484A-155, "the standing of a vehicle ... otherwise than temporarily") both exclude a halt for a passenger or loading exchange; drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration ... A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted") carries the halt with that exclusion read through its length (observable_reading purpose). "No person shall" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"in a roadway" (DEF-NRS-484A-220, "that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder"): st.roadway "the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder" at its whole extent; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Not the sidewalk.

"parallel with the edge of the roadway headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement": the direction of lawful movement of traffic (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, "vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel", whose lawful direction the carrier designates) is st.lane_direction "direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in" of the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the edge of the roadway runs along that direction, so a heading (kin.heading "direction the body points") aligned with it within a tolerance is both parallel with the edge and headed with traffic. The heading is not the direction of motion, and the ruling direction is the carrier's, not the vehicle's.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that stands or parks: drv_motion_parked(subject) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.standing_min_duration, and it occupies a region of kind st.roadway (rel.occupies). Exception: some dev.regulatory_sign with code angle_parking governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: For every travel region l (kind st.travel_region, not an intersection) the subject occupies that carries a designated direction, the subject's heading is aligned with it: kin_heading(subject) dot st_lane_direction(l) is at least p.parked_heading_cos (both read normalised). Unknown where an occupied carrier's direction or the heading is unobserved.

narrowings.why: What the Chapter otherwise provides is read through a posted angle_parking sign governing the subject's travel region; a provision that shows in no posted feature is not read.

The definitions' exclusion of a halt for receiving or discharging passengers or for loading is read through the halt's length: a halt shorter than the standing duration is not standing; "No person shall" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"parallel with the edge of the roadway" is read through the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies, along which the edge runs, rather than through the edge's own outline; parallel within the heading tolerance.
